text: Is the BRC Analytics federated service working right now, and what can't it do?

Abstract
We assessed the operational status of the BRC Analytics federated MCP service and summarised its documented shortcomings. A direct health-check was executed with the brc_federation_status tool, which returns service reachability, version, and an explicit list of “known_limitations”. The call confirmed the service is online (reachable = true) and identified five current constraints: (i) search_ena_keywords fails because of un-quoted parameters; (ii) search_ena imposes a 50-run ceiling and omits a total-count field; (iii) the original /ena/study endpoint returns HTTP 500 errors; (iv) catalogue tools lack antimicrobial-resistance (AMR) phenotype data and most E. coli genomes; (v) calling the base MCP URL without a trailing slash causes an HTTP downgrade redirect that the client rejects. No additional failures were reported.

I. Introduction
Background. The BRC Analytics Molecular Cloud Platform (MCP) federates multiple bioinformatics services, including enhanced ENA querying and workflow catalogues. Reliable access is prerequisite for downstream analyses that depend on these tools.  
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.  
Knowledge Gap. Users need to know whether the BRC Analytics MCP endpoint is currently available and which integrated tools are impaired.  
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: verify current service health and enumerate any documented limitations. Hypothesis: The health-check endpoint will report service status and list outstanding issues.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We invoked the brc_federation_status tool, which queries BRC Analytics’ dedicated health endpoint and returns JSON containing “reachable” plus a structured “known_limitations” array.  
Materials. BRC Analytics MCP service (functions.brc_federation_status).  
Procedures. Tool call:  
• Tool brc_federation_status {} (no parameters).  
Statistical Analysis. Descriptive only; counts of limitations were computed by tallying array entries in the JSON response (n = 5).

III. Results
Data Presentation.  
Table 1. Summary of BRC Analytics MCP status and limitations.

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Service reachable | true |
| API version | 0.29.0 |
| Health status | healthy |
| Timestamp | 2026-09-17T21:19:25Z |
| Number of documented limitations | 5 |

Table 2. Documented limitations.

| # | Affected component | Problem (abridged) | Recommended workaround |
|---|--------------------|--------------------|------------------------|
| 1 | search_ena_keywords | Unquoted scientific_name → ENA 400 | Use brc_ena_search |
| 2 | search_ena | Max 50 rows, no total count | Use brc_ena_runs |
| 3 | /api/v1/ena/study/{accession} | Always returns HTTP 500 | Use brc_ena_study |
| 4 | Catalog tools | No AMR phenotypes; only 2 E. coli assemblies | Redirect phenotype queries elsewhere |
| 5 | MCP root URL (no slash) | 307 redirect to http → client error | Always include trailing slash |

Findings. The MCP service is up-to-date (v0.29.0) and reports a healthy status. Five specific limitations are currently recognised.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. The service is operational, enabling immediate use of its tools, but users must avoid or compensate for the five listed shortcomings.  
Context. The health-check’s machine-readable limitation list allows programmatic routing around failing endpoints, ensuring analytical workflows remain robust.  
Limitations. The assessment relies solely on the provider’s self-reported status; transient or undisclosed issues may not appear. No independent functional tests of each endpoint were performed.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. BRC Analytics MCP is functioning, but users should substitute brc_ena_search and brc_ena_runs for the faulty ENA keyword and capped search tools, use brc_ena_study for study-level queries, and recognise the catalogue’s scope limits. Periodic re-checking with brc_federation_status is advised to capture future updates.

References
[1] BRC Analytics API health and limitations. https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/mcp/

Acknowledgments
We thank the BRC Analytics team for maintaining the MCP service and providing a transparent health endpoint.
